title: Trump Memorandum Targets Late-Transition Federal Bargaining Agreements, Citing Education Department Deal
description_short: Trump's Jan. 31, 2025, memorandum directed agencies not to approve certain late-transition federal bargaining agreements and cited a Jan. 17 Department of Education deal.
description_medium: On January 31, 2025, Trump issued a memorandum directing executive agencies not to approve collective-bargaining agreements made in the 30 days before a presidential transition if they purported to continue under the incoming administration. It cited a Department of Education agreement negotiated January 17. This documents a federal workforce policy; it does not establish the agreement was disapproved or that public-school teachers lost tenure or bargaining rights.
description_long: On January 31, 2025, President Donald Trump issued a memorandum for executive departments and agencies addressing collective-bargaining agreements made near a presidential transition. It states that agreements executed in the 30 days before an incoming president takes office and purporting to continue under the new administration “shall not be approved.” It specifically cites a Department of Education agreement negotiated January 17, 2025, and bars agencies and agency employees from making certain CBAs in the final 30 days before a transition. This is evidence of a federal policy directed at late-transition agreements, including one at the Department of Education; the memorandum does not document whether that agreement was ultimately disapproved. Its text does not change teacher-tenure rules, identify state or local school districts, or establish that public-school teachers lost bargaining rights nationwide. The entry should be limited to the memorandum and its stated federal scope. The available record does not support the original claims that Trump abolished teacher tenure, terminated union contracts nationwide, or implemented the Project 2025 predictions as completed policy.

source_fact_map.source_title: Limiting Lame-Duck Collective Bargaining Agreements That Improperly Attempt To Constrain the New President
source_fact_map.source_date: Memorandum dated January 31, 2025; published February 14, 2025 (90 FR 9581; document 2025-02729).
quotes: Therefore, it is the policy of the executive branch that CBAs executed in the 30 days prior to the inauguration of a new President, and that purport to remain in effect despite the inauguration of a new President and administration, shall not be approved.

In the final days of the prior administration's tenure, it purposefully finalized collective bargaining agreements (CBAs) with Federal employees in an effort to harm my Administration by extending its wasteful and failing policies beyond its time in office. For example, the Department of Education negotiated a CBA on January 17, 2025—3 days before I took office—that generally prohibits the agency from returning remote employees to their offices.
No executive department or agency (agency) or agency employees shall make a CBA governing conditions of employment in the 30 days prior to a change in Presidential administrations that:
A Presidential Document by the Executive Office of the President
supported_facts: The Federal Register identifies the document as a January 31, 2025 presidential memorandum from the Executive Office of the President, published February 14, 2025.
The memorandum directs that certain CBAs executed in the 30 days before a presidential inauguration and intended to remain in force under the new administration shall not be approved.
The memorandum specifically cites a Department of Education CBA negotiated January 17, 2025, concerning employees returning from remote work.
The memorandum addresses federal executive departments, agencies, and agency employees; it does not document whether the cited Department of Education agreement was ultimately disapproved.
limitations: The memorandum does not state that public-school teachers lost tenure or bargaining rights, does not identify state or local school districts, and does not establish a nationwide union ban.
The source establishes the directive and its cited example, not implementation or the ultimate status of the cited agreement.

source_fact_map.source_title: Fact Sheet: President Donald J. Trump Exempts Agencies with National Security Missions from Federal Collective Bargaining Requirements
quotes: President Donald J. Trump signed an Executive Order using authority granted by the Civil Service Reform Act of 1978 (CSRA) to end collective bargaining with Federal unions in the following agencies with national security missions:
- National Defense. Department of Defense, Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), the National Science Foundation (NSF), and Coast Guard.
supported_facts: The White House fact sheet describes a separate March 27 executive order as ending collective bargaining for federal unions in listed agencies with national-security missions.

The list includes the Department of Defense, Department of Veterans Affairs, National Science Foundation, and Coast Guard, among other federal agencies; it does not list the Department of Education or public-school teachers.
limitations: This is a separate federal action and does not show that the January memorandum’s cited Department of Education agreement was disapproved.
The fact sheet concerns federal unions in specified agencies, not state or local public-school teachers.
